reason: Both quotes state continuous backups for point-in-time restore, periodic for long-term retention, and Versioning and Replication for self-recovery from accidental deletions.
The note recommends a lifecycle expiration rule for versioned buckets being backed up because AWS Backup retains all versions and costs might increase.
Quote states a single operation on specified lists, billions of objects per job, progress tracking, notifications and a completion report.
Quotes state the manifest is required, its contents and Inventory/CSV form for a user-generated manifest, and that S3 can generate one from filter criteria.
Quote lists copy, SSE update, tags/ACLs, Glacier Flexible Retrieval restores, Lambda invocation, and custom list or Inventory report.

The quote says live replication replicates newly uploaded objects as they are written and Batch Replication replicates existing objects; it does not say live replication copies 'only' new objects, so the absolute 'only' goes beyond the quote.
Quote states the rule and its condition verbatim.
Quotes recommend not storing credentials in the application or EC2 instance and using an IAM role for temporary credentials for S3 access.
Quote recommends granting only required permissions to reduce risk from errors or malicious intent, in the context of S3 resources.
Quote explains Principal * means anyone and action * allows any action, listed as steps to block public access.
Table row gives EarlyDelete-GDA, GB-Hours, Hourly, prorated storage for Deep Archive deletions before the 180-day minimum.
Table row gives EarlyDelete-ByteHrs, GB-Hours, Hourly, prorated storage for Flexible Retrieval deletions before the 90-day minimum.
Table row gives EarlyDelete-GIR, GB-Hours, Hourly, deleted or transitioned from Glacier Instant Retrieval before the 90-day minimum.
Table row gives EarlyDelete-SIA, GB-Hours, Hourly, Standard-IA deletions before the 30-day minimum.
Quotes support account scope, all Regions and the all-four-settings recommendation, but none says BlockPublicPolicy is best applied at the account level so a bucket-policy editor cannot disable it.
Quote states centralized controls enforced regardless of how resources are created and organization-level enforcement through AWS Organizations.
Quote states the bucket-level default and the recommendation to keep all settings enabled unless a use case needs otherwise.

Quotes support four independent settings, the three levels and the most restrictive combination, and name BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls and RestrictPublicBuckets, but no quote names BlockPublicPolicy as one of the four.
Quotes state the four levels, no per-object support, and that settings do not alter policies or ACLs so removal makes them public again.
Quote states the private default, that users can modify policies to allow public access, and that the settings override them.
Quotes state account inheritance of org policies, most restrictive of bucket and effective account settings, and the protected-bucket example.
Quotes state propagation to selected member accounts, override of account settings, and all four settings applied together at org level.
Quote states bucket ARN instead of object ARN in KMS CloudTrail events and fewer events for SSE-KMS objects.
Quote supports 'up to 99 percent' by decreasing S3-to-KMS traffic, but the stated condition (savings depend on number of requesters, request patterns and object age) is not in the quote.
Quote states that with SSE-KMS default encryption you can enable Bucket Keys to decrease KMS request traffic and reduce cost.
Quotes state the default global namespace, uniqueness across accounts and Regions within a partition, and the account regional namespace option.
Quotes state name and Region cannot be changed after creation and ownership is not transferable.
Quote states no max bucket size or object count, one bucket allowed for all objects, and no bucket inside another bucket.
Quote states the bucket owner can explicitly deny access to objects regardless of owner and can delete any object.
Quote states the restriction and the deny-all example verbatim.
Quote gives this exact bucket policy example.
Quote states Deny with aws:PrincipalOrgID denies principals outside the organization and that Deny overrides any Allow regardless of how granted.

Quotes support the 20 KB limit for bucket and identity-based policies, but not that complex per-object permissions 'need' access points or Access Grants; the page only recommends them for complex requirements.
Quote states permissions apply to objects owned by the bucket owner and not to objects owned by other accounts; context ties other-account ownership to ACLs being enabled.
Quote describes a policy limiting reads to objects with a tag key and value using s3:ExistingObjectTag.
Quote states resource-based IAM policy, owner-only association, and coverage of objects owned by the bucket owner.
Quotes state aws:MultiFactorAuthAge enforces MFA, gives credential age in seconds, and is null when not created with MFA.
Quotes state a policy requiring SSE-KMS on every written object with denial otherwise, and the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption key with AES256 for SSE-S3.
Quotes state aws:SecureTransport, true for HTTPS and false for HTTP, and the example explicitly denies HTTP.
Quotes state deny-all when the endpoint is not used, aws:SourceVpce takes the endpoint ID not an ARN, and console access is disabled.
